messages.text:
Goal: commit Handy to Lane A and write the policy/security/privacy
docs every later prompt will reference.

Files to touch (all new):
- docs/PLAY_POLICY_MATRIX.md (one row per feature: API used, user
  benefit, in-app disclosure copy, confirmation level, risk class,
  Play justification verbatim for the Console).
- docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md (the 11 threats from this plan + mitigations
  table).
- docs/PRIVACY_MODEL.md (data taxonomy + redaction sinks + retention).
- docs/ACTION_POLICY.md (the typed ActionPolicyEngine spec — copy
  Section 10 of HANDY_NEXT_LEVEL_PLAN.md verbatim then expand with
  the per-recipe rules table).

Files to touch (existing):
- Handy_Android_Build_Plan_V2_Scope.md (prepend a "Lane: A — general
  screen-aware AI copilot" header; any later PR that argues Lane B
  must flip it).
- DEBUG_LOG.md.

Do NOT:
- Change Play submission copy yet (PLAY1 does that after Phase 4
  ships).

Acceptance:
- Four docs exist, cross-link each other and HANDY_NEXT_LEVEL_PLAN.md.
- The Plan V2 Scope header names Lane A.
I’ll set the repo’s policy spine in place first: inspect the current plan/log docs, then add the four new docs and prepend the Lane A marker without touching submission copy.

I see the worktree already has local edits and an untracked `docs/` tree, so I’m going to treat those as user-owned and layer only the requested files/headers on top. Next I’m pulling the exact Section 10 and threat list from the plan so the new docs stay anchored to the existing roadmap.

The plan has the exact Phase 4 policy engine block and a ten-row risk register; the eleventh security item is the secure-screen/tap-on-secure-screen threat called out in the metrics and policy rules. I’m going to encode those as explicit docs now, with the Play submission text parked as draft console copy only.

I’m making the docs fairly explicit because later prompts need to be able to point at one stable rule instead of re-litigating Play, privacy, and action safety each time. I’ll also add a short debug-log entry so the repo history explains why these docs landed.
The requested files are in place now. I’m doing a quick acceptance pass: checking the Lane A header, cross-links, and the diff so I can catch any policy-doc typo before handing it back.

Done. Handy is now explicitly Lane A.
